goal: Remove the standalone `kitcode mini` command and `/mini` route, then fold the mini, progress, dynamic-island, and watch-style glance surfaces into switchable view modes inside `kitcode terminal`.

in: Remove `kitcode mini` from public CLI help, command parsing, command dispatch, tracker-unavailable behavior, and package README command documentation.
Remove the public `GET /mini` local route and stop importing or serving the standalone mini renderer.
Stop launching the standalone mini Electron entry; delete or leave unused mini-specific source only if implementation keeps repository references tidy and checks updated.
Keep `kitcode terminal` and `GET /terminal` as the single local window surface for terminal and glance modes.
Add a small terminal view-mode switcher in the upper-right header area, adjacent to the close control.
Support terminal default mode plus fixed glance modes for compact horizontal progress, progress-focused bottom-right panel, dynamic-island top-center view, and watch/swatch top-right widget view.
When switching modes in Electron, resize and reposition the BrowserWindow to the selected preset: terminal centered and resizable, compact/progress bottom-right, island top-center, watch top-right.
Keep every non-terminal mode fixed-size and non-resizable; only terminal mode may be user-resized.
Keep all modes draggable with clear no-drag regions for close and switcher controls.
Render READY, LIVE, IDLE, OFFLINE, and reconnecting states in every glance mode using existing `/api/summary` and `/api/events` data.
Keep the terminal safe-shell command engine, prompt focus, history navigation, dashboard command, and close behavior.
out: No standalone `kitcode mini` command, mini window process, or mini route compatibility shim.
No changes to reward calculation, tier thresholds, redemption logic, equals counting, tracker runtime behavior, or local state persistence.
No new campaign backend, login, claim flow, remote telemetry, or dashboard redesign.
No arbitrary system shell execution from terminal input.
No persistence of last selected view mode unless implementation later receives an explicit product decision.

acceptance_criteria.summary: `kitcode mini` is absent from CLI help and command dispatch; invoking `mini` is treated like an unsupported command rather than opening a window.
The local API no longer exposes `GET /mini`; terminal mode remains available through `GET /terminal` and existing API/event/reward endpoints continue unchanged.
The terminal header renders a compact view-mode switcher near the upper-right close control, with available modes for terminal, compact, progress, island, and watch.

Electron mode changes resize and reposition the same terminal BrowserWindow to the selected preset: terminal centered/resizable, compact and progress bottom-right/fixed, island top-center/fixed, and watch top-right/fixed.
Only terminal mode allows user resizing; compact, progress, island, and watch modes lock minimum and maximum dimensions to their preset size.
Every mode remains draggable, while close and mode switcher controls remain clickable through explicit no-drag regions.
All terminal and glance modes render progress and READY/LIVE/IDLE/OFFLINE/reconnecting states from existing `/api/summary` and `/api/events` data without changing reward or tracker contracts.
Terminal mode continues to behave as a safe KitCode-only terminal and never executes arbitrary shell commands.

coverage_plan.summary: Run the CLI package build script after implementation so command, route, reward, source snapshot, ledger, mini-removal, and terminal checks pass together.
Update CLI command checks so `mini` is no longer advertised or handled as a supported public command, while `terminal` remains supported.
Update terminal window checks to assert the mode switcher, safe command list without standalone mini instructions, shared summary/event usage, and no shell execution hooks.
Add or update a focused source check for terminal Electron mode presets, resizable toggling, min/max locks, top-center/top-right/bottom-right placement math, and drag/no-drag requirements.

Run `kitcode track` and `kitcode terminal`, then verify switching between terminal, compact, progress, island, and watch modes, including placement, fixed sizing, dragging, close behavior, and live state updates.

risks.summary: Removing `kitcode mini` is an intentional breaking change for existing users who launch the mini surface directly.
risks.mitigation: Update help, READMEs, checks, and unsupported-command behavior together so the new single-entry `kitcode terminal` model is explicit.

risks.summary: Browser-side mode switching needs a safe way to request BrowserWindow resize/reposition while keeping node integration disabled and the terminal safe-shell boundary intact.
risks.mitigation: Expose only a narrow mode-change bridge from Electron to the renderer, such as a preload/contextBridge or equivalent allowlisted IPC API for known mode IDs.

risks.summary: Compact, progress, island, and watch modes have very different shapes, increasing the chance of clipped text, overlapping controls, or unreadable state copy.
risks.mitigation: Use fixed dimensions, constrained text, stable progress elements, and source or manual checks for every mode at its preset size.

risks.summary: Bottom-right, top-center, and top-right placement can vary across displays, docks, taskbars, and full-screen work areas.
risks.mitigation: Use the primary display workArea with explicit margins for first implementation and validate manually on desktop.

risks.summary: Removing `/mini` and the `mini` command changes both local HTTP and CLI contracts.
risks.mitigation: Update contract JSON, docs, CLI checks, local route expectations, and package build checks in the same implementation.

implementation_handoff.summary: Consolidate all KitCode glance surfaces into `kitcode terminal` view modes and remove the standalone mini public surface.
suggested_sequence: Remove `mini` from CLI help, public command contract, README command tables, command dispatch, mini URL helper, and standalone Electron launcher.
Remove the `/mini` route and mini renderer import from the local API; update local API contract notes to make `/terminal` the only window HTML route.
Retire or remove mini-specific source/check files, or update package build scripts so obsolete mini checks no longer assert a standalone route/window.
Add a small mode switcher to terminal chrome near the close button and remove safe-shell `mini` command copy that tells users to run `kitcode mini`.
Implement terminal renderer state for `terminal`, `compact`, `progress`, `island`, and `watch`, using existing summary fetch and event stream logic.
Add an allowlisted Electron bridge for mode changes so the renderer can request preset BrowserWindow size, resizable policy, and position without exposing shell or filesystem capabilities.
Define terminal, compact, progress, island, and watch presets in terminal Electron code, including fixed min/max locks for all non-terminal modes and restored resizability for terminal mode.
Keep drag/no-drag regions correct for every mode and ensure close/switcher controls stay clickable.
Update checks, docs, agent contracts/coverage metadata, and run the CLI package build plus manual Electron mode verification.
current_behavior_evidence: packages/kitcode-cli/bin/kitcode.mjs currently advertises `mini`, has `miniUrl`, opens `mini-electron.mjs`, and dispatches an `options.command === 'mini'` branch.
packages/kitcode-cli/src/api.mjs currently imports `renderMiniWindow` and serves `GET /mini` alongside `GET /terminal`.
packages/kitcode-cli/src/terminal-electron.mjs currently opens a centered 960x620 resizable frameless terminal window with sandboxed web preferences.
packages/kitcode-cli/src/terminal-window.mjs currently has a close button but no view-mode switcher, and its safe command list still includes `mini` instructions.

packages/kitcode-cli/src/mini-electron.mjs and packages/kitcode-cli/src/mini-window.mjs currently implement the standalone fixed bottom-right mini panel that this requirement removes as a public surface.
notes: Use English copy in the terminal UI, matching the existing terminal requirement.
Do not persist the last selected mode for this version; default launch should be terminal mode.
If Electron is unavailable and `/terminal` opens in a browser tab, mode switching may change layout in-page but cannot reposition the native browser window.
Keep local-first privacy posture unchanged and do not add telemetry for mode switching.
